about: Attack angles handed to red agents in /purple. Each red agent gets one angle per round so the surface is covered from different directions; agents still report any serious weakness they see. Ids must stay unique. Edit freely — add an angle and the dealer uses it.

angles.name: Injection
angles.how: Trace every place user input reaches an interpreter: SQL/NoSQL queries, shell/OS commands, template engines, LDAP, XPath, eval-like calls. Look for string concatenation into a sink instead of parameterization or escaping.

angles.name: Broken access control
angles.how: Check every protected action: can a user reach another user's object by changing an id (IDOR), hit an admin route without the role, or skip an ownership check? Look for missing or after-the-fact authorization.

angles.name: Authentication & sessions
angles.how: Review login, signup, password reset, token and session handling: weak hashing, missing rate limits, predictable tokens, tokens that never expire, secrets compared non-constant-time, session fixation, missing re-auth on sensitive actions.

angles.name: SSRF & file/path
angles.how: Any user-controlled URL, host, path or filename: server-side request forgery to internal services, path traversal, arbitrary file read/write, unsafe upload (type/location/execution), zip/path handling.

angles.name: Data exposure & secrets
angles.how: Hard-coded secrets/keys/tokens, secrets in logs or error messages, sensitive data over-returned by an API (mass over-fetch), missing output encoding leading to XSS, verbose errors, debug mode on, insecure CORS, missing security headers.

angles.name: Deserialization & parsing
angles.how: Untrusted data fed to pickle/yaml.load/Marshal/native deserializers, XML without entity protection (XXE), prototype pollution, unsafe JSON-to-object mapping (mass assignment), and parser resource exhaustion.

angles.name: Business logic & races
angles.how: Workflow abuse: steps skipped or replayed, negative/overflow quantities, price or role tampering, TOCTOU and concurrency races on shared state (balances, stock, limits), idempotency and double-submit issues.

angles.name: Dependencies & config
angles.how: Manifest and lockfile: known-vulnerable or abandoned packages, dangerous default config, over-broad permissions/scopes, exposed management endpoints, insecure transport, missing input size/time limits enabling DoS.
